findings.explanation: 以下同文 means the remaining certificate wording is the same as the preceding text, the formula being privately imitated in Haruki's room. 'The same honors' invents an honor and breaks the repeated graduation-certificate joke.
findings.japanese:
「卒業証書。
３年Ａ組清水早百合。
…以下同文」
findings.todokanai: "I hereby bestow the graduation certificate to Shimizu Sayuri from Class 3-A, with the same honors."

findings.highlight: if you got chosen without warning
findings.evidenceJa: 断り切れなかったときにも恥をかかずに済むように
findings.explanation: Koharu drafted the speech in case she could not completely refuse the selection. The translation makes her already selected without warning, replacing a contingency about failed refusal with a surprise appointment.
findings.japanese:
「小春のことだから、必死で原稿は作っただろ？
断り切れなかったときにも恥をかかずに済むように」
findings.todokanai: "Knowing you, Koharu, you've desperately prepared the speech already, right? So you wouldn't embarrass yourself if you got chosen without warning."

findings.highlight: whether I would be delivering a message or sending one
findings.evidenceJa: 送られてるのか送ってるのか
findings.explanation: The source contrasts being sent off/receiving the valedictory message with sending it herself. Both English verbs are outgoing, erasing the active-passive reciprocity specifically identified in the approved critical note.
findings.japanese:
「それに、送られてるのか送ってるのか、
よくわからなくなっちゃって…」
findings.todokanai: "And I didn't even know whether I would be delivering a message or sending one…"

findings.highlight: I am truly honored and grateful to be able to speak
findings.evidenceJa: 多数の方々のご臨席を賜り、このように盛大な卒業式を開いて下さったことに、卒業生を代表して感謝申し上げます
findings.explanation: The formal speech thanks the many attendees for their presence and for holding the grand ceremony. The translation instead expresses the speaker's honor and gratitude for being allowed to speak, replacing the object and function of the ceremonial thanks.
findings.japanese:
「本日は、多数の方々のご臨席を賜り、
このように盛大な卒業式を開いて下さったことに、
卒業生を代表して感謝申し上げます」
findings.todokanai: "As the representative for all graduating students, I am truly honored and grateful to be able to speak during this great graduation ceremony today."

findings.explanation: Koharu vows to preserve the friendship she believes in, singular and focused on Mihoko. The translation generalizes the climax of her private letter into all of her trusted relationships.
findings.japanese:
『わたしたちの人生は、ずっと続いていくんだから、
ずっと諦めずに、わたしの信じる友情を、
これからも大切にしていくって誓います』
findings.todokanai: "Because our lives still go on, I will never give up, and I promise to treasure all of my trusted relationships all the more."

findings.highlight: pushes herself past her limits and tries to get a hold of herself
findings.evidenceJa: 強いようで、自分をしっかり持っているようでいて
findings.explanation: The source says Koharu appears strong and self-possessed but actually always wavers. The English changes those apparent traits into effort and overexertion, altering Haruki's concise characterization.
findings.japanese:
強いようで、自分をしっかり持っているようでいて、
実は、いつも迷い、揺れている…
findings.todokanai: She always pushes herself past her limits and tries to get a hold of herself, but the truth is, she's always doubtful and hesitant…

findings.highlight: go to prep school so that you perform better during the second wave of admissions
findings.evidenceJa: 予備校探すか二次募集にでも備えてな
findings.explanation: The source offers alternatives: find a prep school, or prepare for secondary recruitment, then suggests applying to Seisen literature. The translation makes prep school a means of improving in the second wave and says to join the department, changing both the options and the applicant's current status.
findings.japanese:
「あんたは予備校探すか二次募集にでも備えてな。
そうだ、青泉の文芸なんてどう？
あんたの愛しの女の子も受けるらしいよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I think you should go to prep school so that you perform better during the second wave of admissions. That's right, how about you join Seisen's Literature Department? Isn't the girl you like going there as well?"

findings.highlight: "Your work never pays off, Class Rep. You are quite popular with the underclassmen, though."
findings.evidenceJa:
「報われないねぇ委員長。
あんた結構人気あったのに、下級生とかに」
findings.explanation: 報われない is unrequited or unrewarded, while the English steers toward work not paying off.
findings.japanese:
「報われないねぇ委員長。
あんた結構人気あったのに、下級生とかに」
findings.todokanai: "Your work never pays off, Class Rep. You are quite popular with the underclassmen, though."
